plan.summary: How a browser turns a URL into pixels: its processes, navigation and lifecycle, the critical rendering path and compositing, the JavaScript engine, the event loop, storage and the same-origin policy.

prerequisites.bridge: The DOM is the tree of objects the browser builds from HTML.
The list of functions running now, newest on top.

outcomes: Explain which browser process does which job and why sites are isolated.
Explain each step from a navigation to the first paint, and the lifecycle events that follow.
Find and fix render-blocking and parser-blocking resources on a page.
Choose CSS properties that animate on the compositor only.
Predict the order in which tasks, microtasks and rendering steps run.
Choose the right browser storage API and explain what the same-origin policy isolates.

lesson_outline.title: Browser architecture: processes, site isolation and engines
lesson_outline.visual_reason: A browser runs separate processes with different jobs and privileges; a diagram shows which process does what and where one site's renderer sits.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Sort jobs (network requests, layout, GPU drawing, JavaScript) into the process that owns them.

lesson_outline.title: Navigation and the page lifecycle
lesson_outline.visual_reason: A navigation is a fixed sequence followed by lifecycle events and states; a sequence and state diagram shows each step and event in order.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Order the navigation steps and match each lifecycle event to the moment it fires.

experience.override_reason: Standard budget is 10; the selector chose explainer (2). The navigation is one fixed sequence that a sequence diagram shows at no cost, which keeps the budget for the three labs.

lesson_outline.title: The critical rendering path: from bytes to pixels
lesson_outline.visual_reason: Parser-blocking and render-blocking resources delay first paint in different ways; the learner toggles async, defer and media attributes and watches the timeline change.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Toggle script and stylesheet attributes and predict when the first paint happens.

experience.override_reason: Standard budget is 10; the selector chose hybrid (6). Two parameters (script attributes, stylesheet media) drive the lesson, so an interactive lesson with checkpoints is enough.

lesson_outline.title: Rendering pipeline: layout, paint and composite
lesson_outline.visual_reason: Changing a CSS property can trigger layout, paint or only compositing; the learner animates different properties and watches which pipeline stages run each frame.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Pick the CSS property to animate and predict which pipeline stages run each frame.

experience.override_reason: Standard budget is 10; the selector chose hybrid (6). One parameter (the animated property) drives the lesson, so an interactive lesson is enough.

lesson_outline.title: The event loop: tasks, microtasks and rendering
lesson_outline.visual_reason: The order of tasks, microtasks and rendering steps decides when code runs and when the screen updates; the learner steps through code and watches the stack and queues.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Step through setTimeout, Promise and requestAnimationFrame code and predict the log order.

experience.override_reason: Standard budget is 10; the selector chose hybrid (6). The stepper with checkpoints teaches the order; a free simulation adds little for this budget.

lesson_outline.title: Inside the JavaScript engine: JIT, hidden classes and GC
lesson_outline.visual_reason: Code moves through parser, bytecode and optimizing tiers and can fall back on a deopt; an animated flow shows the tiers and the deopt path.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Match each engine stage to what it does and to the code pattern that triggers a deopt.

experience.override_reason: Standard budget is 10; the selector chose explainer (2). An animated flow diagram on the page shows the tiers and the deopt path without a separate video.

lesson_outline.title: Browser storage and the same-origin policy in practice
lesson_outline.visual_reason: Each storage API differs in size, lifetime, sync or async access and scope; a comparison shows which fits a job and what the same-origin policy keeps apart.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Sort app data (session token, offline cache, large files, UI preference) into the right storage API.

experience.override_reason: Standard budget is 10; the selector chose branching (3). A comparison table carries the storage decision; the same-origin policy gets its deep dive in the security phase.

mini_projects.use_case: A developer speeding up a landing page lists which scripts and stylesheets block parsing or rendering, from the saved HTML and a HAR file, and suggests async, defer or media fixes.
A team lead writes a small tool that predicts the log order of setTimeout, Promise and queueMicrotask code, and checks it against Node's real output, to teach new hires the event loop.

capstone.name: page-load inspector CLI
capstone.problem: Before release, a team checks how a page loads; a Node.js CLI reads saved HTML, a HAR file and a Performance trace and reports render-blocking resources, long tasks, layout-triggering animations and storage use against a budget.

known: Roadmap 00.1–00.4 (learning system, workstation, DevTools, extension toolkit)
goals: master frontend engineering end to end from the N1 roadmap
learn visually and by experimenting with simulations

curriculum.scope: How a browser works for a frontend developer: process architecture and site isolation, navigation and lifecycle, critical rendering path, rendering pipeline and compositing, JavaScript engine internals, the event loop, storage and quotas, and the same-origin policy at a glance.

concepts.title: DOM, CSSOM and the render tree
Hidden classes and stable object shapes
Tasks, microtasks and the call stack
Cookies, Web Storage, IndexedDB, Cache API and OPFS
What the same-origin policy isolates and allows

discovery.note: Roots seeded from the items of roadmap section 01.2 and confirmed against the verified sources.

Four research units (docs-browser-internals, docs-engines-storage-origin, repos, gap-01) verified children under each root; gap-01 widened the MDN and V8 entries into documentation sets to stay within the 12-source cap.

Children expanded against the same sources. Inline-cache mechanics, lazy parsing and standalone COOP/COEP have no direct verified source in this run, so the concepts were narrowed to hidden classes and to CORS with cross-origin isolation; the coverage audit may add sources.
